references.text: Describes how the Israelites sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, which directly relates to the warning in Deuteronomy against sacrificing to demons.
Forbids the Israelites from sacrificing to goat-demons, referring to the same practice of offering sacrifices to spiritual beings that are not God.
Paul quotes directly from this verse and warns the Corinthians that the offerings of the Gentiles are made to demons and not to God.
Continues the warning that one cannot have fellowship at both the Lord's table and the table of demons, based on the theme from Deuteronomy.
Revelation describes people who worship demons and idols, reflecting the theme of sacrificing to demons instead of the true God.
The prophet Isaiah refers to those who forsake the Lord and set a table for Gad and Meni, foreign deities that the Israelites had not known before.
Jeremiah speaks about the Israelites' worship of other gods that neither they nor their fathers knew, linking to the theme of new gods.
